title: First time building an app entirely with AI: Did you actually feel proud, or did it feel unearned?
author: HaridMek
selftext: Just curious how everyone else felt when they first built a tool or app using purely AI. Did you feel genuinely proud of what you made, or was there this weird feeling of "well, I didn't really do the work"? For some context: I’m in high school right now. I don’t have money for a premium Claude sub, so I’ve honestly just been juggling a few free accounts to build a personal project. I wanted a specific note taking and drawing app. Stuff like Obsidian felt a bit too complex and didn't really fit my aesthetic, notion is too lag for my phone, and the good premium apps cost money. So I decided to just make my own custom one. All the features and UI ideas were mine (heavily inspired by other apps, obviously), but Claude wrote the code. My loop was basically: generate the code, export it, test it on my phone, find bugs, and repeat. Honestly? I feel incredibly proud and happy seeing an idea in my head turn into a real, functional mobile app that I can actually use. I’m definitely not going to go online and flex about "grinding as a dev" because let's be real, the hardest part was literally just trying to explain exactly what I wanted to the AI, figuring out how to prompt for bug fixes, and waiting for my usage limits to reset lol. (Just to be clear, this isn't an ad or a promo for anything, the app is literally just for me). I'm really curious about your experiences. When was the first time you made an app or game using AI? How old were you, and how did you feel about the whole process? Feel free to share your thoughts!

comments.author: SanFranLocal
comments.body: I was like this is fucking sick! Ive been an engineer for a while before and was just super excited about what i could try buildimg with it

replies.author: HaridMek
replies.body: Do you think learning code is important nowadays? Like the AI is getting better and better. I think it still help our brain think better and understand what the AI doing, but I don't know in the future, the AI is so good that humman only need to produce idea.

replies.author: Varrianda
replies.body: Yes, though I can see why people wouldn’t want to anymore. Software engineers will still build overall the best software even though AI tools let you build with literally 0 knowledge. Maybe in 1-2 years models will ascend, but I think if we’re still mostly talking in plain English with a model, understanding at least how to think programmatically will help.

replies.author: HouseMysterious8172
replies.body:
Build app by self-coding vs AI guiding is 2 different path, imaging building a house instead
1. You need to thought/know about the process of build, then use tools to make it
2. AI is like a machine printing the house, you need to guide it prints one

Outcome is different result for different needs

replies.author: syn_krown
replies.body: For sure knowing how to code helps. If you wanted to create Minecraft for example, would you know to tell the AI to use disk space for unused chunks? Or would that not cross your mind? Cause if you put everything in memory at once, it will end up crashing or running slow. And thats a very basic example imo

comments.author: SanFranLocal
comments.body: Its important to know what the AI is doing i still think. It will do what you ask do if you dont know much you could ask the wrong thing

comments.author: TheUniverseOrNothing
comments.body:
I felt really sad for the corporations that continue to screw us and charge $70 an unfinished game. How are they going to profitable if my $200 subscription can build something more complete than they can with millions?

Think of all the CEO’s that will be out of business if we open game studios that pay all those involved fairly.

Hood Warfare is more fun than Call of Duty for $5. Think of how sad gaming will be if we don’t get a new high quality unique COD every year.

comments.author: SeasawPhilosopher
comments.body: It feels extremely earned, I work 70+ hours a week on my game.

comments.author: C0mm0nVillain
comments.body: I feel like ive still done all the work. Art, environment, UI, HUD music, font etc. So I feel good. AI can do most of the code but I feel proud of what my game looks like and how it plays because I did that.

comments.author: BadassMinh
comments.body: Definitely felt proud, all the ideas are still mine and I still guided the AI in the right direction that I want

comments.author: syn_krown
comments.body: Well, I have been programming for about 20 years, so when I use AI, I am directing it as if I am coding it, then reviewing it. So I do feel proud of the results. I wouldnt feel proud one shooting something though, or leaving decisions to the AI.
